paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't need anybody to defend Him. Israel lost the battle, the Philistines grabbed the ark, and it looked like the other side had won. But the ark sat in Dagon's own temple, and Dagon was the one on his face (1 Samuel 5:3). God was never in trouble. He was just sitting there, and the false god couldn't stay standing next to Him.

Now look at what the Philistines did. They saw Dagon fall, then fall apart, then they saw the tumors, and their answer was to pass the ark down the road like a hot tray of cookies. First Gath, then Ekron, and the Ekronites cried out, "They have brought us the ark of the God of Israel in order to kill us and our people!" (1 Samuel 5:10). They knew His hand was heavy (1 Samuel 5:7), but they only wanted Him to be somebody else's problem. Friend, that's a trap we can fall into too, because it's easy to see God's power and still try to move Him down the road instead of bowing to Him.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Anything we set up beside God, whether it's an idol or just something we're leaning on, can't stand next to Him. Don't get stuck in the Philistines' mistake, shipping God out of your life when He gets too close. Keep your ovens ready and your heart open, because the God who stayed standing in Dagon's temple is worth standing with.
